cards.title: Prioritize site speed fixes before other SEO work
cards.summary: Diagnose page load speed with GTmetrix and PageSpeed Insights, then fix the slowest culprits first because speed drives both rankings and purchase conversions.
cards.use_when: Auditing an online store's technical SEO and deciding what to fix first, especially before investing in content or links.
steps: Run the store's key pages (homepage, top category pages, top PDPs) through GTmetrix and Google PageSpeed Insights. PageSpeed Insights shows mobile and desktop separately — optimize mobile first, since Google indexes mobile-first and most consumer traffic is mobile.

Treat the source's stated thresholds as heuristics, not laws: GTmetrix flags load times over 3 seconds as problematic, and the presenter targets a Google PageSpeed score of at least 80 on both mobile and desktop. A store loading at 1.9 seconds was judged fine; one at 9.3 seconds was judged critically slow and the top priority fix.
If GTmetrix and PageSpeed results disagree, run a third free test (Pingdom Tools) to break the tie.
Read GTmetrix's report of the slowest resources to find culprits — heavy images and videos are the usual suspects on product pages.
Fix in priority order (source's typical high-priority list): serve static assets behind a CDN, compress and modernize images, convert images to WebP, lazy-load below-the-fold media.
Re-test after each fix to confirm the change actually improved load time rather than assuming it did.
You can export the GTmetrix PDF report and feed it to an AI tool to translate technical items into a plain-language fix checklist, or hand the checklist to a developer.
caveats: Load-time numbers vary by test location and network; a single test is not definitive.
The 3-second and 80-score figures are the presenter's practical heuristics, not official Google ranking thresholds.
Fixing speed helps conversion as well as rankings, but the source gives no measured conversion lift for these examples.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Convert and compress product images to WebP
cards.summary: Shrink heavy product images by converting PNG/JPG to WebP or compressing them, which speeds up pages and reduces bounce, without visible quality loss.
cards.use_when: Speeding up a store's category or product pages where oversized images are the identified bottleneck in a speed report.
steps: Identify the culprit files from your speed report — look for image URLs with large transfer sizes (the source example found a 3.3 MB PNG dragging down the page).

Save the original image and convert it to WebP format. WebP was developed by Google to keep sites fast; in the source's side-by-side comparison the PNG and WebP looked practically identical while the WebP was dramatically lighter (3.3 MB down to ~1.8 KB in that example).

Do the conversion with a free online tool like Convertio (choose WebP as the output), or use a plugin/built-in optimizer in your store platform if available — the approach depends on the ecommerce platform/CMS.
Update the page to reference the WebP file and delete the original heavy file so it is no longer served.

If your platform does not accept WebP (some builders do not), fall back to compression instead: run the image through a compressor like TinyPNG (free tier around 10 images/day in the source) to cut file size (the source example saved ~70%).
Confirm the visible image quality is still acceptable before publishing, and re-run the speed test to verify improvement.
caveats: WebP support depends on the platform; verify your builder serves it correctly.
Compression does not always match WebP's savings; both quality and file size should be checked.
The 3.3 MB to 1.8 KB example is one image, not a general promise of that ratio.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Audit title tags, meta descriptions and H1s with a browser extension
cards.summary: Use a free on-page SEO extension (e.g., SEO Wallet) to check each money page's title, meta description, H1 and heading order against clear rules.
cards.use_when: Reviewing on-page SEO across a store's homepage, category pages and top product pages before content or link work.
steps: Install a free on-page audit extension (the source uses SEO Wallet) installed in your browser, then open each important page to see its metadata in the sidebar.
Check the title tag: it should combine what the page offers plus location/brand where relevant (the source's good example: 'mortgage brokers in Michigan, Align Lending').

Check the meta description: add a clear call to action at the end (e.g., 'Apply now', 'Get your free consultation') and keep it within roughly 155 characters — the source ties this to improved click-through from search results.

Check the H1: each page should have only one H1. Use the H1 for the page's main search keyword, not a tagline. The source's bad example ('align your dreams for home ownership') is a tagline nobody searches; the fix is the keyword phrase (e.g., 'mortgage experts in Michigan'). Move taglines to a lower heading.
Check heading order: headings should be sequential (H1 then H2 then H3 then H4). A jump from H2 straight to H4 shows as an error and should be corrected.
Repeat for every important page, not just the homepage. Each should target its own keyword and pass the same checks.
caveats: The source calls these '1% improvements' — important but not an overnight ranking fix.
The exact extension interface and features can change; verify current behavior before relying on it.
Heading-order errors are typically minor; do not let them block higher-impact fixes.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Add schema markup to money pages to clarify page content
cards.summary: Inject JSON-LD structured data (Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, etc.) into key pages so search engines instantly know a page's subject, aiding rankings and rich results.
cards.use_when: Improving how search engines understand a store's homepage, category pages and product pages, especially before or alongside content work.
steps: Check which schema a page already has using your audit extension's structured-data section, or Google's official Rich Results Test. The source found tools can disagree, so cross-check with the Rich Results Test before concluding schema is missing.

Identify the right schema types for the page. Rather than memorizing schema.org's catalog, use an AI assistant with web search: paste the page URL and ask which schemas it needs from an SEO perspective. The source's example returned Organization (or a niche type like Bank/CreditUnion), LocalBusiness, and product-level types like FinancialProduct/MortgageLoan.
Generate the JSON-LD code for the chosen type (e.g., LocalBusiness) and inject it into the page's header. How you do this depends on the CMS — search or ask how for your specific platform.
Apply schema to money pages — the homepage and pages you did transactional research for (categories, key products) — not to every page like About or Contact.
Verify the markup with the Rich Results Test after publishing.
caveats: Schema is not required to rank, but it makes the search engine's job easier; the source reports businesses improving rankings after adding the right schema, without citing specific figures.
The more niche the schema type, the better it can describe the page.
Injection method is platform-specific and must be looked up for your CMS.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Make the first fold instantly communicate offer and next action
cards.summary: Cut above-the-fold ambiguity so visitors immediately grasp what the store sells and the one action to take, because scrolling loses a large share of visitors.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a store homepage, category or landing page hero to raise purchase or lead conversion from existing traffic.
steps: Imagine a first-time visitor: within the first screen they should see clearly what is offered and what to do next. The source contrasts a vague hero ('empowering your dog to success') against a clear one ('Melbourne's #1 dog trainers. Get started.').

Write the headline around a concrete keyword phrase describing the offer (e.g., 'Positive dog training for obedience, reactivity and anxiety'), not a slogan. Add a short subline explaining the benefit.
Add one obvious, visible call to action in the hero (e.g., 'Book a consultation', 'Shop now').

Reduce multiple competing CTAs: the source cites the paradox of choice — many options cause indecision. Concentrate on one primary conversion action even if you sell several services/categories, using the hero to route to the main one.
Verify with heatmapping tools (Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity) which the source says show declining engagement as users scroll — the more you force scrolling before clarity, the more visitors you lose.

For a fast audit, capture a full-page screenshot (e.g., with the GoFullPage extension as PNG) and paste it with the URL into an AI assistant to critique the first fold. The source's AI critique independently flagged the vague hero, missing CTA and need for a clear value proposition.
caveats: The 'paradox of choice' and clarity arguments are the presenter's opinion and general CRO principle, not a measured result for the cited sites.
Conversion rates vary widely by niche; the source declines to give a universal target number (1%, 2%, 3% all appear across niches).
AI critiques of screenshots are suggestions, not validated winners — test changes before trusting them.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Win backlinks via journalist-source matching (Featured) as free outreach
cards.summary: Earn high-quality editorial backlinks by answering journalist questions on platforms like Featured (formerly HARO), prioritizing relevance and real experience.
cards.use_when: Building free, relevant backlinks to a store's category or content pages when budget is limited but time is available.
steps: Create a free account on Featured. The free tier allowed roughly three answers per month in the source; paid tiers allow more.
Open the questions tab, clear all categories, and scan publisher requests for ones matching your expertise and store niche.
Save promising questions to answer later, then return to your saved list.

Before answering, vet the publisher's domain authority with a free tool (e.g., Ahrefs' free website authority checker). The source's example, MarketingSherpa, had authority ~83 and was topically relevant to the presenter.
Write a detailed answer drawing on your own first-hand experience — the source stresses that personal experience is what sets you apart from other respondents.
Submit; expect the answer to sit 'in review' until the publisher reads and (if they like it) publishes it, which is when you get the backlink.
Set a recurring monthly reminder to spend your free answers, since publisher requests cycle constantly.
caveats: You only get a backlink if the publisher chooses to publish your answer — not guaranteed.
Domain authority tools are not absolute sources of truth; treat them as rough signals.
Relevance to your niche matters more than raw authority.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Judge backlink quality: relevance over quantity and natural link growth
cards.summary: Prefer one relevant link from a reputable site over many spammy ones, and screen prospects for unnatural referring-domain spikes.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to buy, accept or build a backlink, and vetting any link-building vendor or prospect.
steps: Weight relevance heavily: a link should come from a site in your industry, locality or niche. A dog-training site should not chase links from computer-gaming gear sites, since contextual relevance is what carries value.
Reject quantity-based pitches. If someone offers '1,000 backlinks for $100/$1,000', the source's advice is to walk away — bad-quality links can associate your site with bad neighborhoods.

Vet any prospect with an SEO tool (Ahrefs, Semrush, Moz). Look at the referring-domains trend versus organic traffic. A gradual, natural climb over years is a good sign (the source's example grew steadily).
Flag sudden, aggressive spikes in referring domains as suspicious. The source allows that a viral article can cause a legitimate spike, but says to find the responsible link before trusting it.
Treat cheap link packages as a trigger for due diligence, not automatic disqualification — the source says cheap is not always bad but warrants scrutiny.
For competitive niches, compare your backlink profile to competitors in your initial research; if they have dramatically more links, a backlink strategy is likely necessary.
caveats: Backlink effects take roughly 3–6 months to show, unlike paid search, making ROI hard to attribute.
The source notes agencies often just resell bought links, so outsourcing does not guarantee quality.
The source is affiliated with/paid by one vendor (Get Me Links) and says so; treat vendor recommendations accordingly.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Buy backlinks from vetted vendors when competitors outrank you
cards.summary: If a competitive niche demands links and organic outreach is too slow, purchase links from reputable vendors with relevant industry packages and track them by anchor, target URL and source.
cards.use_when: Considering paid link building for a store in a competitive niche where competitors clearly dominate backlinks.
steps: Confirm the need first: in your competitor research, if rivals have roughly 10x your backlinks alongside much more traffic and leads, paid link building may be justified (the source's framing).
Choose reputable vendors rather than cheap packages. The source names Get Me Links (a vendor it is affiliated with) and The Hoth as two it has used, disclosing its affiliation with Get Me Links.
Use the vendor's strategy call/consultation to get recommendations for your site before committing; the source says these calls are risk-free and educational.
Pick packages segmented by your industry — the source notes vendors split offerings by industry precisely because industry relevance matters.
Track each delivered link by anchor text, target URL and the linking site, so you can judge relevance and monitor the profile over time.
Expect a long lag: the source says backlink ROI takes roughly 3–6 months, unlike paid channels that show results immediately.
caveats: The presenter is an affiliate of Get Me Links and says so — recommendation is not neutral.
Paid links are not cheap, and results are slow and hard to attribute.
Treat vendor guarantees skeptically; the source emphasizes reputable sourcing rather than guaranteed rankings.

Editorial qualification: paid placements must use rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow"; do not buy unqualified links to manipulate rankings. Assess sponsored placements by relevant referral traffic and commercial value, not promised ranking credit.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Separate Search Console (how Google sees you) from Analytics (what visitors do)
cards.summary: Use Search Console for rankings, queries and indexing, and Analytics for traffic sources and on-site behavior — pulling the two apart stops metric confusion.
cards.use_when: Setting up or interpreting search and site performance data for an online store to decide next actions.
steps: Understand the split: Google Search Console shows what your site ranks for, average position, click-through rate from search results, and indexing problems — 'how Google sees my site'. Google Analytics shows where visitors come from (not only Google) and what they do after landing — 'what users do on the site'.
In Search Console, watch three query categories: your brand name (you should rank for it; if not, that is a problem), product/service keywords, and informational keywords you target with content.
Use the Pages report to diagnose pages that are not indexed — the source notes crawling does not guarantee indexing, and non-indexed pages can explain low traffic.
Use Analytics to compare traffic sources and, crucially, quality/conversion, not just volume. Inspect referral sources and investigate any that send high-quality engaged traffic.
Export Search Console or Analytics data (CSV/Sheets) and feed it into an AI analyst tool or a dashboard (Looker Studio template) if you cannot interpret it manually.
Act on only the numbers you can act on — the source repeatedly warns against analysis paralysis and ignoring vanity metrics.
caveats: Average position in Search Console is approximate; personalized location can shift actual results, so it is not exact.
Analytics needs correct tracking; 'unassigned' sources indicate missing attribution.
Set up of both tools assumes property configuration, which is outside this card.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Mine positions 9–30 in Search Console for low-hanging SEO wins
cards.summary: Find pages already ranking on page 2+ and improve them with updated content, internal links or targeted backlinks, which is faster than ranking new pages.
cards.use_when: Planning the next month's SEO work on a store's existing pages when you are unsure where to start.
steps: In Google Search Console, open the Pages report, sort by average position, and increase rows shown (the source uses ~50 rows).

Filter to pages sitting roughly in positions 9–30. The source calls positions ~9–10 'low-hanging fruit' because they are already indexed and getting some traffic, just not ranking well (page 2 of results).
For each such page, choose a remedy: improve the page content/title, build supporting content that links to it, or point backlinks directly at it.
Prioritize these over brand-new pages, because you start from an already-indexed, already-crawling asset rather than zero.

Use an AI analyst (the source's custom GPT over Search Console data) to surface these opportunities automatically — the presenter notes the tool independently flagged positions 11–30 and suggested CTR and featured-snippet improvements.
Build a recurring monthly review so this becomes a repeatable process rather than a one-off.
caveats: The 9–30 band is the source's practical heuristic, not a fixed rule.
Improvements still take time and are not guaranteed to move the page.
Position bands can overlap with what the presenter also labels as '11 to 30' opportunities; treat them as the same broad bucket.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Use Analytics traffic-source data to find partner and acquisition opportunities
cards.summary: Examine which referral and channel sources send quality converting traffic, then deepen or replicate those sources rather than chasing raw volume.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest acquisition or partnership effort for an online store by reviewing real source performance.
steps: In Google Analytics, go to Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition for the last 28 days to see channels (direct, organic search, organic social, paid, referral, etc.).
Drill into Source/Medium for more detail on individual referrers.

Compare not just traffic volume but quality: look at engagement/bounce, time on site and especially conversions per source. The source stresses that a source with less traffic can produce more conversions than a high-volume one.

Investigate strong referral sources. In the source example, a PC-part site sent a lot of good-quality traffic (about 45 seconds average session) to a PC retailer — the recommendation was to reach out to that site for a closer partnership.

Check the tech/device breakdown (roughly quarterly) to spot imbalance — e.g., if desktop dominates traffic but mobile converts better (or vice versa), investigate the underperforming device experience and fix it.
Use the insight to allocate next month's effort toward channels/sources already proven to convert, rather than diversifying blindly.
caveats: Traffic volume is not quality; a big source can still fail to convert, so always pair volume with conversion data.
Attribution can be imperfect ('unassigned'), so treat source labels cautiously.
The partner-outreach example is illustrative, not a guaranteed outcome.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Ignore domain authority as a vanity metric; judge by keywords and conversions
cards.summary: Domain authority/ranking is a third-party composite that does not map to the bottom line, so track rankings for target keywords and actual conversions instead.
cards.use_when: Choosing which SEO KPIs to report or optimize when evaluating a store's website performance.
steps: Recognize domain authority is a proprietary score from tools like Moz (and similar metrics from Semrush, DataForSEO), each calculated differently — it is not an official Google metric and not a reliable proxy for results.
Note the source's point that high-domain-authority sites do not necessarily convert, so the number alone is misleading as a success measure.
Track instead: the number of keywords the site actually ranks for and, ultimately, conversions (form submits, orders) — the source calls this the real aim.

When reporting SEO progress to stakeholders, frame improvements in traffic and conversions rather than ranking jumps alone; the presenter notes agencies (including himself) historically over-celebrated ranking moves that did not affect the bottom line.
Do not treat domain authority as useless — use it at most as a rough comparative signal in link prospecting, not as a performance target.
caveats: Source explicitly calls out its own former over-focus on rankings as a mistake, framing this as an opinion and best-practice shift.
Rankings can still be a useful leading indicator even if not the final goal.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Turn raw SEO data into actions with an AI analyst
cards.summary: Export Search Console/Analytics data and feed it to an AI analyst to get prioritized, actionable recommendations and seasonal patterns instead of drowning in spreadsheets.
cards.use_when: Monthly SEO review for an online store when you have the data but are unsure what to do with it.
steps: In Search Console (or Analytics), select the last 28 days and export the report (CSV or Google Sheet).
Load the exported data into an AI analyst tool set up for Search Console/Analytics data.

Ask it specifically for low-hanging opportunities (e.g., pages in positions 11–30), CTR improvements, featured-snippet opportunities, and hidden gems — the source's tool produced exactly this structure.
Use the output to build a prioritized to-do list rather than doing exploratory analysis yourself.

Look for seasonal patterns the data reveals — the source notes a PC retailer whose traffic rose with each new GPU launch — and plan content or promotions around recurring demand peaks; likewise, seasonal businesses (e.g., landscaping in winter) can see slow periods in the data.
Refresh this monthly as a standing habit instead of ad-hoc digging.
caveats: AI recommendations must be sanity-checked and tested, not applied blindly.
Data quality depends on correct tracking and indexing.
The source used a specific custom GPT tool; functionality of AI tools changes, so verify the current setup.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Beware automating SEO before fundamentals work
cards.summary: Automation can amplify broken SEO, so validate fundamentals (technical health, content, conversion) before scaling with workflow tools.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in SEO automation tooling for an online store.
steps: Before automating, confirm fundamentals are sound: site speed, indexing, on-page metadata, working schema and a converting first fold for the key pages.
Understand the source's warning: 'just because everything can be automated doesn't mean it should be' — scaling without fundamentals produces worse outcomes.
If fundamentals are ready, choose an automation platform. The source names three it has used, with Pabbly called the easiest plug-and-play for no-code automation.
Map a small number of high-value, repetitive SEO tasks to automate first (e.g., report pulling, content brief assembly) rather than everything at once.
Test each automation on a small scope before letting it run broadly, to catch errors before they scale.
Re-check the tools' current interfaces and capabilities before building, since automation platforms change frequently.
caveats: Source's tool preferences and 'easiest' ranking are personal experience, not independent benchmarks.
Over-automation is explicitly flagged as a failure mode in real cases the presenter observed.
cards.source_name: Complete SEO Course (3 Hours)_ Rank #1 AI Search _ Prompts Included.docx

cards.title: Add a CTA to meta descriptions and differentiate from competitors in the SERP
cards.summary: Improve click-through from search results by adding a within-limit call to action and standing out from competing snippets, a lever before rankings improve.
cards.use_when: Ecommerce SEO where pages rank but get few clicks, or while waiting for ranking gains and wanting more clicks from current positions.
steps: Draft a meta description containing a clear call to action at the end (e.g., 'Apply now', 'Get your free consultation') and keep it within about 155 characters.

Inspect the current search results page for your target keyword; deliberately write a description that differs from competitors' snippets so yours stands out, which the source says can sharply raise click-through.
Allow a natural, human tone rather than keyword stuffing — the source prefers descriptions that read naturally.
Pair the description change with an SERP title/tag optimization, then measure CTR in Search Console before and after.

Layer further testing: the source suggests tools like Microsoft Clarity (behavior) and VWO (A/B testing) to test one change at a time, such as CTA wording — e.g., 'Submit your free form' vs 'Call now'.
Test only one element per experiment so you can attribute the effect.
caveats: The click-through improvement claim comes from the presenter's own experience, without a stated measured benchmark.
Whether Google displays your exact meta description is not guaranteed; it may rewrite it.
Character limits are guidance, not strictly enforced.
